column1: Elderly people are growing healthier, happier and more independent, say American scientists.
column2: 美国科学家表示，老年人正变得越来越健康、快乐且独立。

column1: The results of a 14-year study to be announced later this month reveal that the diseases associated with old age are afflicting fewer and fewer people and when they do strike, it is much later in life.
column2: 一项历时14年的研究将于本月晚些时候公布结果。结果显示，受老年相关疾病困扰的人越来越少，即使发病，发病年龄也比过去晚得多。
column5: later this month|本月晚些时候
column11: much later in life|在人生中晚得多的时候

column1: In the last 14 years, the National Long-term Health Care Survey has gathered data on the health and lifestyles of more than 20,000 men and women over 65.
column2: 在过去的14年里，全国长期健康护理调查项目共收集了超过2万名65岁以上老年人健康和生活方式的相关数据。

column1: Researchers, now analysing the results of data gathered in 1994, say arthritis, high blood pressure and circulation problems — the major medical complaints in this age group — are troubling a smaller proportion every year.
column2: 研究人员正在分析1994年收集的数据。他们说，关节炎、高血压和血液循环问题，是这个年龄段最主要的健康问题。受这几种疾病困扰的人所占的比例逐年下降。
column8: circulation problems|n. 血液循环问题
column9: major medical complaints|n. 最主要的健康问题

column1: And the data confirms that the rate at which these diseases are declining continues to accelerate.
column2: 数据也证实，这些疾病在人群中所占的比例下降得越来越快。

column1: Other diseases of old age - dementia, stroke, arteriosclerosis and emphysema - are also troubling fewer and fewer people.
column2: 痴呆、中风、动脉硬化和肺气肿等其他老年病，困扰的人也越来越少。
column3: diseases of old age|n. 老年病

column1: ‘It really raises the question of what should be considered normal ageing,’ says Kenneth Manton, a demographer from Duke University in North Carolina.
column2: “这确实引发了这样一个问题：什么才应该被视为正常的衰老过程呢？”北卡罗来纳州杜克大学的人口学家肯尼思·曼顿说道。

column1: He says the problems doctors accepted as normal in a 65-year-old in 1982 are often not appearing until people are 70 or 75.
column2: 他说，1982年医生认为在65岁的人身上属正常的那些问题，现在往往要到70岁或75岁才出现。

column1: Clearly, certain diseases are beating a retreat in the face of medical advances.
column2: 显然，随着医学进步，某些疾病正逐渐减少。
column5: beating a retreat|逐渐退却或减少

column1: But there may be other contributing factors.
column2: 但可能还有其他促成因素。

column1: Improvements in childhood nutrition in the first quarter of the twentieth century, for example, gave today’s elderly people a better start in life than their predecessors.
column2: 例如，在20世纪头25年里，儿童营养的改善使今天这代老年人的人生起点好于前辈。
column5: first quarter|n. 最初的四分之一
column8: better start in life|更好的人生起点

column1: On the downside, the data also reveals failures in public health that have caused surges in some illnesses.
column2: 不利的是，这些数据还揭示了公共卫生方面的缺陷，这些缺陷导致了某些疾病的激增。

column1: An increase in some cancers and bronchitis may reflect changing smoking habits and poorer air quality, say the researchers.
column2: 研究人员指出，某些癌症和支气管炎的发病率上升，可能与吸烟习惯的变化以及空气质量恶化有关。

column1: ‘These may be subtle influences,’ says Manton, ‘but our subjects have been exposed to worse and worse pollution for over 60 years.
column2: “这些因素的影响也许并不明显，”曼顿说，“但我们的研究对象在六十多年里一直暴露在日益严重的污染中。
column6: have been exposed to|一直处在……影响下
column7: worse and worse|越来越严重的

column1: It’s not surprising we see some effect.’
column2: 我们能看到一些影响，并不奇怪。”

column1: One interesting correlation Manton uncovered is that better-educated people are likely to live longer.
column2: 曼顿发现了一项有意思的关联：受教育程度较高的人往往更长寿。
column5: better-educated|adj. 受教育程度较高的

column1: For example, 65-year-old women with fewer than eight years of schooling are expected, on average, to live to 82.
column2: 例如，受教育不足八年的65岁女性，预计平均能活到82岁。

column1: Those who continued their education live an extra seven years.
column2: 那些继续接受教育的人能够多活七年时间。

column1: Although some of this can be attributed to a higher income, Manton believes it is mainly because educated people seek more medical attention.
column2: 收入较高可以解释其中的一部分差异，但曼顿认为，主要原因是受过教育的人更常就医。
column7: educated people|n. 受过教育的人
column8: seek more medical attention|更常就医

column1: The survey also assessed how independent people over 65 were, and again found a striking trend.
column2: 调查还评估了65岁以上人群独立生活的程度，同样发现了一个引人注目的趋势。

column1: Almost 80% of those in the 1994 survey could complete everyday activities ranging from eating and dressing unaided to complex tasks such as cooking and managing their finances.
column2: 在1994年的受访者中，近80%能完成各类日常活动，从自己吃饭、穿衣，到做饭、理财这样较为复杂的事情。
column13: managing their finances|料理个人财务

column1: That represents a significant drop in the number of disabled old people in the population.
column2: 这表明，人口中失能老年人的数量显著减少了。
column6: disabled old people|n. 失能老年人

column1: If the trends apparent in the United States 14 years ago had continued, researchers calculate there would be an additional one million disabled elderly people in today’s population.
column2: 据研究人员推算，如果美国14年前显现的趋势延续至今，今天还会多出100万名失能老人。
column10: disabled elderly people|n. 失能老年人

column1: According to Manton, slowing the trend has saved the United States government’s Medicare system more than $200 billion, suggesting that the greying of America’s population may prove less of a financial burden than expected.
column2: 曼顿说，这一趋势的放缓已为美国政府的联邦医疗保险计划节省了2000多亿美元。这表明，美国人口老龄化带来的财政负担可能比预想的轻。
column6: Medicare system|n. 美国联邦医疗保险计划

column1: The increasing self-reliance of many elderly people is probably linked to a massive increase in the use of simple home medical aids.
column2: 许多老年人越来越能自理，这可能与家用简易医疗辅助器具的使用大幅增加有关。
column9: home medical aids|n. 家用医疗辅助器具

column1: For instance, the use of raised toilet seats has more than doubled since the start of the study, and the use of bath seats has grown by more than 50%.
column2: 例如，跟研究刚开始时相比，加高马桶座圈的使用量已超过原来的两倍，洗澡椅的使用量则增加了50%以上。
column4: raised toilet seats|n. 加高的马桶座圈
column5: more than doubled|增至原来的两倍以上

column1: These developments also bring some health benefits, according to a report from the MacArthur Foundation’s research group on successful ageing.
column2: 根据麦克阿瑟基金会关于‘成功老龄化’研究小组的报告，这些发展也带来了一些健康上的益处。

column1: The group found that those elderly people who were able to retain a sense of independence were more likely to stay healthy in old age.
column2: 该研究发现，那些能够保持独立感的老年人更可能在晚年保持健康。

column1: Maintaining a level of daily physical activity may help mental functioning, says Carl Cotman, a neuroscientist at the University of California at Irvine.
column2: 加州大学欧文分校的神经科学家卡尔·科特曼说，每天保持一定的体力活动，可能有益于心智功能。
column4: daily physical activity|n. 日常体力活动

column1: He found that rats that exercise on a treadmill have raised levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor coursing through their brains.
column2: 他发现，在跑步机上运动的大鼠，脑内流动的脑源性神经营养因子水平较高。
column7: brain-derived neurotrophic factor|n. 脑源性神经营养因子

column1: Cotman believes this hormone, which keeps neurons functioning, may prevent the brains of active humans from deteriorating.
column2: 科特曼认为，这种能够维持神经元正常功能的激素，或许能够防止活跃人群的大脑功能逐渐衰退。

column1: As part of the same study, Teresa Seeman, a social epidemiologist at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles, found a connection between self-esteem and stress in people over 70.
column2: 在同一项研究中，来自洛杉矶南加州大学的社会流行病学家特蕾莎·塞曼发现，70岁以上的人群中，自尊心与压力之间存在关联。

column1: In laboratory simulations of challenging activities such as driving, those who felt in control of their lives pumped out lower levels of stress hormones such as cortisol.
column2: 在模拟驾驶等具有挑战性的活动的实验中，那些认为能够掌控自己生活的人，会分泌较少的应激激素，比如皮质醇。

column1: Chronically high levels of these hormones have been linked to heart disease.
column2: 这些激素长期高水平存在与心脏病有关。

column1: But independence can have drawbacks.
column2: 但独立也可能有弊端。

column1: Seeman found that elderly people who felt emotionally isolated maintained higher levels of stress hormones even when asleep.
column2: 塞曼发现，那些感到情感孤立的老年人，即使在睡眠状态下，体内的压力激素水平仍然较高。

column1: The research suggests that older people fare best when they feel independent but know they can get help when they need it.
column2: 研究表明，老年人如果觉得自己能独立生活，同时知道需要时有人帮忙，状态就最好。
column7: when they need it|在需要帮助时

column1: ‘Like much research into ageing, these results support common sense,’ says Seeman.
column2: 塞曼说：“这与许多有关老龄化的研究一样，研究结果印证了常识。”

column1: They also show that we may be underestimating the impact of these simple factors.
column2: 研究还表明，我们可能低估了这些简单因素所产生的影响。

column1: ‘The sort of thing that your grandmother always told you turns out to be right on target,’ she says.
column2: 她说：“你祖母常跟你讲的那些道理，到头来还真说对了。”
